props.doc:
Build the canvas: an SVG layer for wires under a DOM layer for nodes.

Wires are SVG because they need to be curves that hit-test cleanly. Nodes are
DOM because they need to be focusable, readable by a screen reader, and
styleable by the same stylesheet as the rest of the workspace. Drawing nodes
into the SVG would have been less code and would have made them unreachable
by keyboard.
props.name: createCanvas

props.doc:
One node: header, summary, and a port row.

The badges are the point of the whole editor. A node that will change the
estate says so before you run it, a node that needs an approval says so, and
a response node says what fraction of the estate it actually reaches. All
three are read off the registry, not typed in by whoever drew the playbook.
props.name: renderNode

Drag a node, drag from a port to connect, drag the background to pan, wheel
to zoom.

Pointer events rather than mouse events, so this works with a trackpad, a
pen and a touchscreen without three code paths. Pointer capture means a drag
that leaves the window still ends cleanly.

props.doc:
Keyboard on the canvas.

Arrow keys nudge, Delete removes, Ctrl+Z/Y undo and redo, Ctrl+S saves the
draft, F frames the graph, Escape clears the selection. A SOC engineer
building a playbook should not have to reach for the mouse for any of these.
props.name: attachKeyHandlers
